claims.text: Increasing Mn concentration in magnetic high-entropy alloys will increase the coercive field.
The Mn ions being added are magnetic.
The proposed effect applies to magnetic high-entropy alloys across varying Mn concentrations.
The proposed Mn-induced coercivity increase should hold at room temperature and standard atmospheric conditions.
The relevant high-entropy alloys have a spinel structure.
Increasing Mn concentration increases spin frustration in the magnetic lattice.
A higher degree of spin frustration produces a higher coercive field.
The Mn-enriched alloy will have a higher coercive field than an otherwise matched alloy without the Mn increase.
There is a maximum Mn concentration that can be incorporated without changing the material's structural properties.
The relationship between Mn concentration and coercive field is not well understood.
The Mn–coercivity relationship may depend on the specific composition of the high-entropy alloy.

contradictions.description: The material is repeatedly described as a high-entropy alloy, while the stated spinel mediator is characteristic of oxide/ferrite systems. No oxygen-containing high-entropy oxide is specified.
